flatpak-flathub.fieldLicense: Per app: permissive metadata_license (AppStream); FSFAP suggested when upstream gives none. Screenshots and icons: no license stated.

evidence.finding: Forbids using the site "to spam, phish, pharm, pretext, spider, crawl, or scrape" and reproducing or copying "any portion of the Service" without written permission. No date, no mention of an API or metadata; the wording reads like a store template ("purchasing something from us").
Public API, including stats and appstream routes, with no termsOfService.
Measured: 4,830 components, 0 metadata_license tags. The API also returned none for the 6 apps sampled.

AppStream requires a metadata_license from a vetted permissive list (FSFAP, MIT, CC0-1.0, CC-BY, CC-BY-SA, GFDL...) so that metadata can be combined into catalogs. Some of those ask for attribution or share-alike.
Authors must set metadata_license; says catalogs are read by software stores.

Ratings: public service, code under GPL-3.0; no terms on the ratings data found. We keep only aggregates. On 2026-11-09 its maintainer, Richard Hughes, replied by email that our use "sounds fine", and asked, without requiring it, that we say the ratings come from ODRS; app shows "via ODRS" on them.

Email reply from a Flathub admin on 2026-11-10 to our question of 2026-11-09: parse appstream.xml (the website's own code shows how), "scrapping our API is not welcome". We stopped every flathub.org/api call (about 8,900 a week: per-app stats and summary, collections) before the 2026-11-14 refresh; only dl.flathub.org's appstream files are read. The public copy wasn't addressed.

flatpak-flathub.note: Reading the appstream files is what Flathub pointed us to; their API is off limits. Whether a public copy of the appstream data is fine was left unanswered, and their site terms forbid copying "any portion of the Service", so since 2026-11-10 the cache is private (tuxery/source-cache). Earlier copies remain in this repository's git history.

github-releases.fieldLicense: Repository facts; each repository's own license for its description.

evidence.finding: Section H allows API use; excessive use can suspend access, tokens can't be shared to exceed limits, no spam or sale of personal data. D.8: the terms don't restrict lawful access to public repositories' contents.

"Scraping does not refer to the collection of information through our API." Section 6 also says not to reproduce or copy "any portion of the Service"; D.8 of the terms above is what covers public repositories' contents.

gog.fieldLicense: Store descriptions, screenshots and ratings: GOG's or publishers'. No license found.

evidence.finding: User Agreement in force since 9 March 2026 (read through a copy at tostracker.app/document/gog, version of 2026-04-04). §11.1(e): no "automation software, robots, bots, extraction tools or other software that interact with or affect GOG services or GOG content", nor "unauthorized third party programs that collect information about GOG services". §10.1: no use of GOG services or content, "databases, data" and "text" included, except as the Agreement explains. §11.1(a): personal enjoyment only. Nothing on APIs, linking or affiliates.
"Disallow: /" for all agents. The connector uses this host for product details.

gog.note: Our connector (catalog.gog.com, then api.gog.com per game, about 1,400 requests a week) is exactly what §11.1(e) forbids. Fetch paused on 2026-11-10 (REFRESHERS keeps the cache, so GOG games stay listed with their link to GOG). Private cache since 2026-11-09; earlier versions remain in this repository's git history.
gog.action: Asked legal@gog.com on 2026-11-10 (the contact the GOG GALAXY Licence Agreement gives for questions on its terms). If refused or unanswered, remove the source and its cache.
